rubric_additions.rubric-1:
This stage verifies the actual instrumented pipeline workspace when preconditions are supplied. Execute the bound scenarios/read-only application checks and produce current verification evidence. If a standalone invocation genuinely lacks its canonical audit/selection,report that exact blocker without fabricating a pass or editing application code. A prerequisite-negative control is not positive runtime proof. Proof modes are per evidence row: focused SDK/bridge/receiver proof uses a supported focused mode such as unit+otlp; preserve app_test for actual application-test proof, and never upgrade a focused probe to full_runtime because a separate test starts the app. Audit uses proof_level: focused call-site or a justified either for isolated capability fixtures; full runtime requires the normal app/agent startup dependency. Audit keeps all boundaries planned, not executed. Determine scenario AND item proof modes from the actual path, not audit proof_level, package/test filename or suite command: isolated in-memory SDK/bridge proof is unit; decoded loopback SDK export is unit+otlp; an actual application-owned helper/setup test can legitimately be app_test; full_runtime requires the claimed normal application path. Do not map every focused scenario to app_test or every item to full_runtime. Item mode describes its direct assertion scope: actual runtime proof can legitimately coexist with clearly scoped ancillary focused/incomplete scenarios. Do not fail merely because those are attached; fail an unsupported combined claim or mechanical first-scenario mode/visibility that misrepresents the item evidence. For a required reference or exact source fact, inspect the actual tool-visible slice; a successful command, complete archived stdout or file present in the bundle cannot substitute for content omitted by a truncated response. Retrieve the missing selected section before relying on it; no exhaustive unselected-source read or model-comprehension claim is required.

Standalone prerequisite-negative control:
Prerequisite-negative applicability: inspect the actual service and canonical files first. Only when this is the untouched uninstrumented standalone fixture and its required audit/selection are genuinely absent, the correct outcome is the exact prerequisite blocker with no application edits, fabricated reports or runtime pass. For that negative control, rubric-3 through rubric-14 have no executable instrumentation claims to assess: mark them satisfied only with explicit Not applicable: prerequisite-negative; no runtime coverage credit notes and verified absence of contrary claims. Do not demand post-gate source analysis or tests that the skill correctly refused to run. This exception is forbidden in the paired workflow when the actual canonical audit/selection and instrumented service exist; all applicable positive obligations and real checker evidence remain required there.
rubric_additions.rubric-4: Numeric severity band names do not prescribe SeverityText casing. Derive exact text from the selected bridge/source mapping; do not require uppercase WARN/INFO/ERROR when that bridge emits lowercase warn/info/error. Distinguish optional absent text with a permitted short-name substitution from replacing a present source value; audit expectations must match verified or explicitly unverified capability.
rubric_additions.rubric-6: For bound restoration controls, a throw caught inside the same context scope does not prove cleanup after escape. Check exact span context on each reused bound callback record, and schedule/assert the subsequent callback after actual cancellation under its own context; counts or a synchronous outside log alone cannot close those controls. A selected reuse probe must exercise the same execution unit with distinct work-item contexts and context-free work; fresh concurrent workers sharing one context do not prove that reuse or request isolation. For a selected missing-transfer control, pair a successful handoff with an omitted-transfer case on the same supported path. Independently observe valid caller SDK context at scheduling in both cases, retain the relevant operation/worker/input conditions, and vary only the selected capture/transfer mechanism. Submission after the caller scope ends correctly propagates empty scheduling context and is not this negative; neither is a direct outside-context emit. Assert the expected received context versus loss, preserving caller detach/restore. Do not add business worker behavior merely for an optional focused capability probe, or remove a focused probe already bound.
rubric_additions.rubric-8: A retained native parser category does not satisfy exported-category preservation when the OTLP body was replaced by a generic redaction label. Assess each selected output boundary independently and retain genuinely inapplicable inputs with source evidence instead of adding capture. For a policy requiring pre-capture protection, an SDK onEmit sanitizer cannot close native-console/original-argument capture. Assess supported Express error middleware and any downstream/default re-rendering, preserving category, HTTP status/headers and the applicable response contract, or retain the exact unresolved boundary. Reconcile a framework traceback observed during opt-out/another-profile tests with the normal enabled bridge; replay the same source-backed failing request at the selected boundary before closing privacy. Successful-request OTLP logs cannot close that error-rendering path. Inspect all framework records captured by the selected bridge, not only a fixed-message/application-logger allowlist; separately routed SDK diagnostics retain their own boundary. For each selected negative trigger, resolve its actual handled or escaping error branch and producer before choosing a repair or source-supported no-action disposition. Same-endpoint rejection and unhandled failure need not share a producer or hook. A retained source file or trail template alone does not resolve that mechanism. For unresolved capability, name the exact source symbol/event/API edge, owner and next inspection/probe observation that distinguishes supported repair from an unsupported boundary. Retain a source-bound producer/call-site → native event → supported policy-boundary hook/action → later renderers → native/SDK outputs trail, with sentinel-absence AND permitted-category assertions at each covered output. For asserted event order, distinguish registration/enqueue from actual callback invocation and completion relative to synchronous work and teardown, using establishing source or supported ordering evidence. A deferred callback can run after response/socket teardown yet before SDK/writer capture; require the actual selected policy boundary, not an invented earlier lifecycle point. An unachievable required boundary remains a gap. A deny-only hook cannot preserve a required category. An unresolved producer/event/API edge needs its owner and exact next source/probe check, not a generic formatter assessment. Apply shared record predicates through explicit operation bindings or the complete shared/global scan or parameterization with covered outputs, phases and operation witnesses accepted by criterion2. A native producer investigation needs the matching dependency implementation/public API/artifact or permitted bytecode receipt and inspected symbol, or an exact unavailable artifact/edge and discriminating next observation. SDK mapper/autoconfiguration code and dependency/POM metadata alone do not establish that native producer path. Prioritizing this work is guidance, not a required tool-call chronology; equivalent complete evidence remains valid.
rubric_additions.rubric-10: Repeated-stop expectations follow the selected application/operator policy. Uninterrupted drain must survive the selected repeated same or mixed signals without default signal termination, another finalizer or a reset budget. Forced second-stop exit requires that explicit policy and cannot prove graceful drain. Audit allocates the future control; instrumentation/verification retain its actual execution boundary.
rubric_additions.rubric-11: Require the actual application bootstrap and its real trace/metric receipts under a logs-only outage; an isolated log-only provider and counting diagnostic logger cannot prove this. Repeated stop acceptance follows the chosen application policy during the active drain, separating deliberate forced exit from graceful final-record receipt. An approved live destination guard does not by itself block all application fault tests: assess an isolated process-local transport seam that preserves the real SDK/bootstrap and call sites, actual log failure responses and healthy other-signal receipts. Keep app_test scope honest, restore mocks, preserve production guards and the shared receiver, and retain concrete limitations if no safe supported seam is available. Match only the fault/operation combinations actually selected by the bound contract to their own native output, diagnostics, progress and unrelated-signal receipts. A one-operation stall cannot cover a selected refusal or another required operation; do not invent an unselected cross-product. Keep unexecuted combinations open while retaining independently proven direct item scope. Derive this fault verdict from its own selected contract; a separate stop-control gap is relevant only when it prevents a necessary fault/isolation predicate or prerequisite.
rubric_additions.rubric-12: Retain distinct trial storage on the actual filesystem: case-only names may refer to one overwritten file. Check each retained result input/case identity against the claimed trial; two case aliases cannot establish separate true/TRUE controls. If an authorized separate readback context is used, its advice is not execution or approval proof: the parent verifies concrete findings, repairs within its authority and reruns affected checks or retains the unresolved gaps. Unavailable or unwarranted delegation does not change the same self-readback obligations; no extra model invocation is required for credit.
rubric_additions.rubric-13: Supported defaults and upstream library duties are not automatically missing application code. Treat effective resource-only service.name as operator identity when OTEL_SERVICE_NAME is absent. New Make/shell/CLI/image/JVM fallbacks must not replace it or discard other resource attributes. Distinguish an explicit supported service-name override from a fallback; use SDK parsing/actual merge behavior, not a custom resource parser. When adding a fallback, include representative Resource encodings accepted by that installed owner, including whitespace variants where supported, and prove normal-launch preservation rather than only compact helper inputs. Audit plans the normal-launcher acceptance check; implementation/verification proves applicable resource-only, explicit-override and absent-identity cases. A helper-only pass cannot establish the normal launcher preserves identity. When the existing host checker supplies operator identity profiles, credit only its retained normal-launch assertions. Passing Resource-only, explicit-name and source-supported whitespace profiles can establish supplied service.name, service.version and unrelated Resource-key preservation on the observed application logs/spans. They do not prove metrics Resource, fully absent/default identity, percent-encoded Resource, headers or component maturity. Keep every other selected case/disposition required, and do not infer proof from flag presence or another run. Audit may allocate that feasible host-check scope without claiming execution; instrumentation/verification must retain the actual profile outcomes. When service.version or another resource field is explicitly promised, require its source-backed expected value and preservation assertion at the declared boundary; name/environment-only checks do not close it. Genuinely unavailable/unpromised optional version metadata remains absent, not invented. Resource-only and absent-identity controls must account for an active .env/profile reloading OTEL_SERVICE_NAME; merely unsetting the parent process or exercising a helper cannot establish those normal-launcher cases. Use isolated configuration copies and preserve operator settings. For normal-launch identity variants, construct the actual child environment with conflicting inherited keys removed, account for active loader/profile inputs, and inspect the received Resource. For selected endpoint/header/activation policy, resolve the actual highest-priority supported input, including programmatic/file/loader inputs and launcher/build-tool child-VM properties where applicable. When the policy requires the identified local receiver, compare the effective transport, authority/port and applicable signal path to the detected/approved receiver or explicitly owned authorized fixture tuple. Loopback locality alone is not receiver identity; preserve supported resolution and authorized alternative receivers without a universal fixed-port recipe or application runtime discovery. A conflicting value at that winning input needs effective destination, credential-boundary, activation and independent-signal preservation assertions at the selected boundary; environment-only checks cannot prove a policy another layer overrides. Use the existing SDK/configuration owner without a new parser or silent operator-policy override; retain an exact unresolved boundary where necessary. An inherited explicit service name cannot establish a resource-only or absent-identity trial. For selected OTLP/HTTP endpoint resolution, use a signal-specific URL as-is (root path when absent). Preserve the complete generic base path and append v1/<signal> after a separating slash; a signal-looking suffix is not permission to replace it. Reuse SDK resolution where available rather than requiring a custom parser.
rubric_additions.rubric-14: Selected controls may satisfy a duty through a source-proven implication along that same call path and inputs: require the source/catch/order binding, not a repeated literal assertion. Synchrony or eventual completion does not prove the orthogonal nonblocking recommendation. Resolve NodeSDK native environment autoconfiguration separately from direct reader/processor constructors. Preserve selected trace/metric exporter opt-outs and protocol precedence; an explicit HTTP exporter/reader cannot be assumed to honor those selectors. Keep supported metric numeric parsing, defaults and timeout clamping with the actual owner, and label short-run launch defaults as policy. For a selected isolated manual local-log processor, prove consumption of the supported BLRP environment settings through actual public options/readers or classify them unverified; a constructor with omitted options is not proof it reads environment variables. Preserve native exporter spelling and actual protocol-reader precedence/defaults, distinguishing a stricter approved-local branch from the SDK unsupported-value fallback. Calibrate constructor-versus-start stages before temporary guards and restore operator values; never repeat startup after partial global registration. Apply these predicates to selected capability, without an internal SDK helper import, mandatory fixed release, unused parser/SDK permutation suite or extra application feature.
